industry: Life insurance (term, whole, final expense, mortgage protection, juvenile; agents, agencies, direct carriers)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'No medical exam' without the adjacent, equal-prominence disclosure that issue may depend on health answers, when issue isn't guaranteed (NAIC 570 Sec. 5C).
'Low cost' / 'inexpensive' for guaranteed-issue products (5H); 'free insurance' for a reduced first premium (5T(3)).
'Immediate coverage' / 'guaranteed acceptance' if benefits are graded or there's a waiting period, unless the limitation is prominent (5G).

'Funeral Expenses', 'Final Supplemental Plan', 'Death Benefits Update', 'Federal Benefit Information', 'Medicare', 'Social Security' or seals/eagles in a way that implies government connection (42 USC 1320b-10; disclaimers don't cure it).
Unsourced statistics, e.g., gold 008 'Average funeral costs are between $7,000-$10,000' (5R requires source; FTC Sec. 5).
Calling a product something other than life insurance (5D); 'financial planner' titles for insurance-only producers (5N).
'Pennies a day' / '<$1/day' unless it's a real premium for a stated age/health/amount (gold 022 uses a female-31 example).
Unaudited vendor results quoted as fact.
compliance_notes: NAIC Model 570 as adopted by the state governs life ads: insurer named (Sec. 6A); policy type described (5E); graded benefits and non-level premiums prominently described; testimonials genuine with paid relationships disclosed; statistics sourced; insurers keep ad files 5 years (Sec. 9).

42 USC 1320b-10 bans words/emblems implying Social Security/Medicare/government connection, including 'Funeral Expenses', 'Final Supplemental Plan' and 'Death Benefits Update'; up to $5,000 per violation, each piece separately; disclaimers don't cure.
39 USC 3001(h): government look-alike mail is nonmailable without the required disclaimers.
Producer license disclosure (e.g., CA Ins. Code 1725.5); state unfair trade practices (NAIC 880) and anti-rebating limits on gifts (seminar meals/donuts are inducements - check state cap).
Reply-card leads: follow-up calls are subject to TSR/TCPA/state rules (not researched here).
Juvenile life: marketing to parents only; avoid implying school endorsement (570 Sec. 5S student rules are analogous).
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, status, relief, nostalgia are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.
No age/demographic angle unless a cited source supports it for this industry; even then, check Fair Housing / ECOA before using it in housing or credit.

emotion_by_offer.why: Cost overestimation is the main barrier (LIMRA 2025).
headline_offer_patterns: 'Most people guess wrong. Here's the real price.'
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Bedtime story with a young parent.
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Teaser prices without the qualifiers; '$15/mo' with no age/health/amount; 'pennies a day' gimmicks.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 005/006/010 'no medical exam, immediate coverage' vs NAIC 570 5C/5G
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: keep the ease benefit, add the adjacent health-questions disclosure and prominent graded-benefit limits.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 008 'Average funeral costs are between $7,000-$10,000' vs NAIC 570 5R and FTC Sec. 5
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: no unsourced stats; use a current sourced figure supplied by the client or drop it.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Final-expense mail commonly styled like benefit notices vs 42 USC 1320b-10
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: no 'Final Supplemental Plan', 'Funeral Expenses' or 'Death Benefits Update' framing, no seals; disclaimers don't fix it.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold '$15/mo for $250k' headlines (001/007/014) vs LIMRA evidence that a real price corrects overestimation
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Both point the same way, but law sets the form: keep a specific price, add age/health/term/insurer qualifiers next to it.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: LIMRA reports bigger need gaps among some racial and income groups vs standing rule on demographics
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Standing rule wins for creative: no race/income angle. Use LIMRA's age-linked cost misperception only where it applies (young families), as an evidence-based exception.
